assumptions.statement: Resource Pressure Index is a normalized screening indicator and is not an estimate of litres of water required or saved.
Resource Pressure Index combines water stress and climate risk using a 60/40 weighting.
The 60/40 weighting is a transparent project-design choice and has not been statistically optimized or externally validated.
Heat exposure is screened using daily maximum temperature when raw temperature data are available.
A rainfall value below 1 mm/day is treated as a dry-day screening indicator.
High integrated risk is defined as an integrated risk score of 50 or greater, consistent with Phase 14.
Very high integrated risk is defined as an integrated risk score of 75 or greater.
Scenario comparisons represent methodological crop-health scenarios and do not establish causal field outcomes.
No actual financial savings are estimated because farm-specific cost, yield, labor, and intervention data are unavailable.
No actual water savings are estimated because measured baseline and post-intervention water-use data are unavailable.
No carbon reduction is estimated because defensible farm-level activity data and emission factors are not part of the current dataset.
Impact indicators should be interpreted as screening-level exposure and resource-pressure indicators.
